notes: Behavior was preserved in all six runs: every hidden test passes with and without the skill. The six assertions the baseline failed are all about process and reporting (separate commits, pins committed before cuts, test command named, evidence on every finding, the env override offered for removal).

The baseline removed more code: 79% vs 56% of the export feature, 70% vs 57% of pricing. In the diff case the skill's 'delete; do not rewrite' left three one-method exporter classes in place. In the feature case the gap is the cache (47 lines) and the config (18) that the skill run held back as tier B.

Both cutting prompts say 'apply the safe cuts, list the rest', which hands the baseline the skill's central idea. A prompt that only says 'simplify this' would test whether the baseline holds back contract changes on its own.

Two grader bugs were fixed after the runs and before scoring. (1) A hidden test required export_tasks('yaml') to raise ValueError, an input the CLI cannot produce; both runs changed it. (2) An assertion required the quote cache to be gone, but both runs found it carries load: an unhashable sku gets 'bad request' only because the cache key cannot be hashed.

Not asserted: the skill runs left durable pins (14 and 59 tests) on a branch with one commit per cut; the baselines left changes uncommitted and the tests as thin as before. On the repo case the baseline proposed adding a validation and rewriting two classes; the skill run reported the bugs and declined the rewrite.
All four cutting runs, with and without the skill, compared old against new code on generated inputs without being told to. That is a technique the skill should name.
Cost of the skill: about +31% tokens and +15% wall-clock.
